text: And while we're on the topic, studies show that men are twice as likely as women to not wash their hands after they use the restroom, and of the ones who do wash their hands, 50% don't even use soap. So do with that information what you will. So the lady in this video claims that studies show men are twice as likely as women not to wash their hands after using the restroom, and that around half of the men who do wash their hands do not even use soap. Now, this video comes from a blogger I'm not exactly a big fan of, because she often makes some pretty crazy and sensational claims. But again, guys, your personal emotions should not stand in front of your objectivity. And as much as I don't want to, I have to concede this one. She is basically right. In one 2013 observational study, researchers watched 3,749 people using public restrooms. They found that 14.6% of men did not wash their hands at all, compared with 7.1% of women. So in that particular study, men were indeed just over twice as likely as women to leave without washing their hands. The second part is also mostly correct, although she phrases it slightly inaccurately. The study found that only 50.3% of all men observed washed their hands with soap. Around 35% used only water, while almost 15% didn't wash at all. So it's not exactly that half of the men who washed their hands did not use soap. It is that almost half of all the men observed did not use soap. Either because they used only water or didn't wash their hands at all. I know it's a bit confusing. Now, to be fair, one observational study conducted in one American college town is fairly weak evidence on its own. You cannot observe a few thousand people in one location and confidently conclude that men everywhere are exactly twice as likely as women not to wash their hands. But unfortunately for us, this was not the only study to find this pattern. A larger series of observations conducted at public attractions across several American cities found that in 2005, 90% of women washed their hands compared with 75% of men. In 2007, it was 88% of women compared with only 66% of men. And in 2010, it was 93% of women compared with 77% of men. There was also a massive British study that used electronic sensors to monitor soap use during around 198,000 restroom visits. It found that approximately 65% of women used soap compared with only 32% of men. So the precise claim that men are twice as likely should not be treated as some universal scientific rule. That particular number comes from one study. But the broader claim that men are less likely than women to wash their hands properly is supported by several different observational studies. So yes, I may not particularly like the messenger, but in this case, the general message is supported by the evidence. And guys, hygiene is important. Wash your hands after using the restroom. And also, use soap. This should not even be controversial. It is basic hygiene.
